ontologyNodes.name: Substance
ontologyNodes.definition: The primary sense of "being" (*to on*); that which is neither said of nor in a subject; what a thing fundamentally is. Analyzed across the Metaphysics through four candidate criteria (essence, universal, genus, substratum) and resolved in Z.xvii as form (εἶδος) — the cause by reason of which matter is some determinate thing. Primary in formula, in order of knowledge, and in time over all other categories. In Lambda, three kinds: sensible-perishable, sensible-eternal, immovable.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Complete Works; Aristotle - Metaphysics; Aristotle - Physics

ontologyNodes.name: Form
ontologyNodes.definition: The determinate structure or actuality that makes matter into a "this" (*tode ti*). Not itself generated — only the composite comes into being (Z.viii). Identified as substance in the primary sense at Z.xvii: form is the cause by reason of which matter is some definite thing. Distinguished from Platonic Forms (separately existing universals) as immanent and individual. In Lambda, that which is simple and actual is first in the column of substance.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Complete Works; Aristotle - Metaphysics; Aristotle - Physics

ontologyNodes.name: Matter
ontologyNodes.definition: That out of which a thing comes to be and which persists; the substratum capable of receiving form; the capacity for being and not-being in each generated thing. In Delta, the primary immanent constituent. In Epsilon, the cause of the accidental. In Zeta, the ultimate substratum when all predicates are stripped away — but lacking separability and *tode ti*, hence not substance in the primary sense. In Eta, matter and form are "one and the same thing, the one potentially, the other actually." The unmoved mover (Lambda) is without matter.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Complete Works; Aristotle - Metaphysics; Aristotle - Physics

ontologyNodes.name: Actuality
ontologyNodes.definition: The existence of a thing not in the way expressed by "potentially"; defined by analogy, not by genus (Theta.6): as building is to the capacity to build, so the waking to the sleeping. Prior to potentiality in formula, in time (for the species), and in substance (Theta.8). Complete actualities (seeing, thinking) are distinguished from incomplete movements (learning, building) by the tense test. The unmoved mover's very substance is pure actuality. Etymologically derived from *ergon* (deed/work) and extended to *entelecheia*.

ontologyNodes.name: Potentiality
ontologyNodes.definition: A starting-point of change in another or in the self qua other. Three-grade schema in De Anima (first potentiality, first actuality/hexis, second actuality). In the Physics, the potential infinite. In Metaphysics, rational vs. non-rational potentialities.

ontologyNodes.name: Fulfillment
ontologyNodes.definition: Used interchangeably with *energeia* in many passages. Etymologically "having-its-end-within" (from *telos* + *echein*). The word *energeia* is derived from *ergon* and extended to *entelecheia* (Theta.8, 1050a21-23). Central to the De Anima definition of soul as "first entelecheia of a natural body that has life potentially."

ontologyNodes.name: Movement/Change
ontologyNodes.definition: The actuality of the potential qua potential. In the Physics, the central object of investigation. In De Anima, phantasia defined as a kinesis. In On Memory, chains of residual movements constitute memory and recollection. In Movement of Animals, desire is the proximate cause of animal locomotion.

ontologyNodes.name: Perception
ontologyNodes.definition: The transition from potentiality to actuality through the agency of an external sensible object; receives sensible forms without matter. The foundational psychological faculty, presupposed by phantasia, memory, and animal movement.

ontologyNodes.name: Imagination
ontologyNodes.definition: A movement resulting from actual sensation. In De Anima, distinct from perception, opinion, and knowledge; subdivided into sensitive and deliberative. In the Rhetoric, the psychological faculty presupposed by "setting before the eyes." In On Memory, the faculty that produces phantasmata on which memory depends. In Movement of Animals, presents objects to desire.

ontologyNodes.name: Intellect
ontologyNodes.definition: The thinking part of the soul; impassible, unmixed, without nature of its own. Never thinks without an image. Active nous is separable, immortal, eternal. In the Metaphysics, divine thought is the activity of the unmoved mover.

ontologyNodes.name: Cause
ontologyNodes.definition: That which accounts for a thing's being, spoken of in four senses: (1) material — that from which a thing comes to be; (2) formal — the formula or pattern; (3) efficient — the primary source of change; (4) final — the "that for the sake of which." Book Alpha surveys predecessors against this framework; Delta.2 provides the lexical analysis; Z.xvii identifies substance with the formal cause. The scheme is presented as exhaustive — no predecessor identified a fifth cause.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Complete Works; Aristotle - Metaphysics; Aristotle - Physics

ontologyNodes.name: End/Purpose
ontologyNodes.definition: The "that for the sake of which." In the Metaphysics, actuality is the end. In the Physics, nature acts for an end. In De Anima, all natural bodies are organs of soul. The formal and final causes often coincide.

ontologyNodes.name: Nature
ontologyNodes.definition: An internal principle or cause of being moved and of being at rest in that to which it belongs primarily, in virtue of itself and not accidentally (192b20--23). Identified in two senses: (1) as matter — the primary underlying substrate; (2) as form — the shape specified in the definition. Form is the more proper sense, since actuality is prior to potentiality (193b6--8).
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Complete Works; Aristotle - Metaphysics; Aristotle - Physics

ontologyNodes.name: Soul
ontologyNodes.definition: The first actuality of a natural organized body having life potentially. Cause in three senses: efficient, final, formal. The central concept of De Anima, presupposed by all Parva Naturalia and Movement of Animals. In the Physics, time qua numbered may require soul as counter.

ontologyNodes.name: Desire
ontologyNodes.definition: That which is moved toward the good. The unmoved mover produces motion *as* the object of desire (Lambda.7). Desire is consequent on thinking, not vice versa. In Theta.5, desire/choice (*proairesis*) determines which contrary a rational potentiality actualizes.

ontologyNodes.name: Logos
ontologyNodes.definition: Polysemous: definitional formula, rational account, ratio, speech, argument-proof. In the Metaphysics, parts of the logos are parts of the form. In De Anima, sense as a logos/ratio between contraries. In the Rhetoric, the third technical proof (demonstration through the speech).

ontologyNodes.name: Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: The faculty of observing available means of persuasion; counterpart of dialectic. The domain-defining concept of the Rhetoric that connects to dialectic, ethics, and psychology.

ontologyNodes.name: Means of Persuasion
ontologyNodes.definition: The means by which persuasion is effected; divided into technical (ethos, pathos, logos) and non-technical. The enthymeme and example are the two modes of demonstrative pistis.

ontologyNodes.name: Enthymeme
ontologyNodes.definition: The rhetorical syllogism; "the body of persuasion." Drawn from probabilities and signs. Twenty-eight lines catalogued.

ontologyNodes.name: Emotion
ontologyNodes.definition: In the Rhetoric, feelings that change judgement, attended by pain or pleasure. In De Anima, the affections of soul are enmattered logoi. In the Metaphysics, Delta.21 gives four senses.

ontologyNodes.name: Essence
ontologyNodes.definition: What a thing is said to be in virtue of itself; the definitional formula of a substance. Belongs primarily and simply to substance; for other categories, definition requires addition. Each primary, self-subsistent thing is identical with its essence (Z.vi). The imperfect tense (*en*) is debated: some read it as logical (not temporal).

ontologyNodes.name: Character
ontologyNodes.definition: In the Rhetoric, the first technical proof: persuasion through the speaker's projected character. Three sources of trust: good sense, excellence, goodwill.

ontologyNodes.name: Style
ontologyNodes.definition: The manner of linguistic expression. Excellence consists in clarity through current words combined with distinction through metaphor. Governed by appropriateness.

ontologyNodes.name: Metaphor
ontologyNodes.definition: The transfer of an alien name; the supreme instrument of prose style. Achieves highest effect through energeia (setting before the eyes). Implies intuitive perception of similarity in dissimilars.

ontologyNodes.name: Setting Before the Eyes
ontologyNodes.definition: Metaphor that represents things in a state of activity, producing quasi-perceptual experience in the audience. The culmination of the Rhetoric's metaphor theory.

ontologyNodes.name: Image
ontologyNodes.definition: The product of phantasia; persists after sensation ceases. In De Anima, quasi-perceptual content for thinking ("the soul never thinks without a phantasma"). In On Memory, the medium of memory with dual nature (object of contemplation and likeness).

ontologyNodes.name: Common Sense
ontologyNodes.definition: The faculty that discriminates between objects of different senses; numerically one but divisible in being. Perceives time. In On Memory, the primary perceptive faculty to which memory belongs.

ontologyNodes.name: Art/Craft
ontologyNodes.definition: Universal knowledge arising from experience; knows the "why." In the Physics, principle in the maker (contrasted with nature's internal principle). In the Rhetoric, rhetoric is a techne. In the Metaphysics, one of three sources of generation.

ontologyNodes.name: State/Disposition
ontologyNodes.definition: A disposition by which a thing is well or ill disposed. In the Rhetoric, rhetoric and virtue are hexeis. In De Anima, first actuality = hexis (possession). In the Metaphysics, the primary contrariety is hexis vs. steresis. In On Memory, memory is a hexis.

ontologyNodes.name: Place
ontologyNodes.definition: "The innermost motionless boundary of what contains" a body (IV.4, 212a20). Not form, not matter, not the extension between containing extremities. Place has "power" (dunamis): each element is carried to its proper natural place (208b10).

ontologyNodes.name: Time
ontologyNodes.definition: "The number of motion in respect of the before and after" (IV.11, 219b1--2). Time is not motion but motion insofar as it admits of enumeration. Time is continuous (as magnitude and motion are). Time is both made continuous by the 'now' and divided at it (220a5).

ontologyNodes.name: The Now
ontologyNodes.definition: The indivisible boundary of time. Same in substratum but different in being (IV.11, 219b12--15). As connecting, it makes time continuous; as dividing, it makes time countable (IV.12, 220a5). Analogous to the geometrical point.

ontologyNodes.name: Privation
ontologyNodes.definition: Absence of an attribute in something that might naturally possess it (Delta.22). The primary contrariety is state vs. privation (Iota.4). In Lambda, one of three principles of sensible substance alongside form and matter. The rational formula explains contraries because it explains both the state and its privation (Theta.2). Contrariety = complete privation.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Complete Works; Aristotle - Metaphysics; Aristotle - Physics

ontologyNodes.name: Principle
ontologyNodes.definition: The first point from which a thing is, comes to be, or is known. All causes are archai. In On Memory, the starting-point of recollective search.

ontologyNodes.name: Practical Wisdom
ontologyNodes.definition: Good sense; one of three sources of trust in the speaker's character. Links rhetoric to the ethical doctrine.

ontologyNodes.name: Colour
ontologyNodes.definition: The limit of the transparent in determinately bounded bodies. White and black are extremes; intermediate colours arise by ratio-mixture. Central to Sense and Sensibilia and On Colours.

ontologyNodes.name: Memory
ontologyNodes.definition: A state or affection of perception/conception, conditioned by the lapse of time, directed exclusively at the past. Belongs to the primary faculty of sense-perception.

ontologyNodes.name: Recollection
ontologyNodes.definition: A quasi-inferential process of recovering memory through deliberate sequential reactivation of habitual movements. Belongs only to beings with the deliberative faculty.

ontologyNodes.name: The Transparent
ontologyNodes.definition: A common nature and power subsisting in all bodies; when actualized by fire it is light. Colour exists at its limit. The medium of vision.

ontologyNodes.name: Being qua Being
ontologyNodes.definition: The subject-matter of first philosophy: being investigated not as some particular kind (physical, mathematical) but in respect of its own nature (Gamma.1). All senses of "being" refer to substance via focal meaning. The inquiry into being qua being asks: what are the first principles and highest causes of being as such?

ontologyNodes.name: The Composite
ontologyNodes.definition: The compound of form and matter — what is generated in coming-to-be: Callias, this bronze sphere. The only kind of substance that is generated and destroyed (Eta.1). Dismissed as "posterior and obvious" in Z.iii, but it is the *tode ti* par excellence. The tension between the priority of form (Z.xvii) and the primacy of the individual composite (Categories) is a standing interpretive problem.

ontologyNodes.name: Truth
ontologyNodes.definition: Reinterpreted from correspondence (adequatio) to unconcealment (Unverborgenheit). Primordial truth is Dasein's disclosedness — the clearing in which entities can be uncovered. Propositional truth (assertion as "true") is derivative, grounded in the more primordial Being-uncovering (Entdeckend-sein). Truth and untruth belong together: Dasein is equiprimordially in truth and in untruth (falling covers over). Truth must be "wrested" from concealment.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Complete Works; Aristotle - Metaphysics; Heidegger - Being and Time

ontologyNodes.name: ψυχή
ontologyNodes.definition: The first actuality of a natural organized body having life potentially (*entelecheia hē prōtē sōmatos phusikou organikou*); cause of the living body in three senses (efficient, final, formal); the central definiendum of the entire treatise.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Movement of Animals; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: αἴσθησις
ontologyNodes.definition: The process by which a sense-faculty transitions from potentiality to actuality through the agency of an external object; receives sensible forms without matter; organized into proper, common, and incidental objects.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Movement of Animals; Aristotle - Sense and Sensibilia

ontologyNodes.name: φαντασία
ontologyNodes.definition: A movement resulting from an actual exercise of a power of sense (*kinēsis hupo tēs aisthēseōs tēs kat' energeian gignomenē*); distinct from perception, opinion, and knowledge; can be true or false; etymologically derived from *phaos* (light). Subdivided into sensitive (*aisthētikē*) and deliberative (*bouleutikē*).
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Movement of Animals; Aristotle - On Memory; Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: νοῦς
ontologyNodes.definition: The thinking part of the soul; must be impassible, unmixed, and without nature of its own to know all things; potentially identical with its objects; the soul never thinks without an image (*phantasma*). Divided into active (separable, immortal, eternal) and passive (perishable).
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ἐντελέχεια
ontologyNodes.definition: Technical term for soul's relation to body; soul is *first* actuality (possession, *hexis*), distinguished from *second* actuality (exercise, *energeia*). The sleeping/waking analogy: soul is to body as sight is to the eye.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: δύναμις
ontologyNodes.definition: Three-grade schema applied to perception: (1) first potentiality (capacity to learn), (2) second potentiality / first actuality (*hexis* -- knowledge possessed), (3) second actuality (active exercise). Body is matter = potentiality to soul's form = actuality.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ἐνέργεια
ontologyNodes.definition: The representation of things as active or alive; the mechanism by which metaphor produces visualization. Homer gives "metaphorical life to lifeless things." In the Rhetoric, ἐνέργεια names the rhetorical effect of vividness, distinct from (but related to) its metaphysical sense.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: κίνησις
ontologyNodes.definition: In Book I: the mark predecessors attribute to soul (refuted -- soul is not a self-mover). In Book III: phantasia is *defined as* a kinēsis; animal movement originates from appetite + practical thought/imagination.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Movement of Animals; Aristotle - On Memory; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: εἶδος
ontologyNodes.definition: Soul is substance as form of a natural body having life potentially; sense receives the *eidos* of objects without their matter (wax-signet analogy).

ontologyNodes.name: ὕλη
ontologyNodes.definition: Body is matter/potentiality to soul's form/actuality; sense receives form *without* matter; plants are affected by forms *with* matter (hence no perception).

ontologyNodes.name: οὐσία
ontologyNodes.definition: Being, beingness, the being of a being; "basic concept of Aristotelian philosophy"; Heidegger renders as "being-there" in existential contexts. Five being-characters from Met. Δ8.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: φάντασμα
ontologyNodes.definition: The sensory image that serves as the medium of memory; has a dual nature — simultaneously an object of contemplation in itself (θεώρημα) and a likeness (εἰκών) of the thing remembered; memory consists in perceiving it *qua* likeness.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - On Memory

ontologyNodes.name: ὄρεξις
ontologyNodes.definition: The genus of motivating states encompassing appetite (ἐπιθυμία), spirit (θυμός), and wish (βούλησις); the proximate efficient cause of all animal locomotion; desire is "the last in the chain of things moved to move something else" (701a1).
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Movement of Animals

ontologyNodes.name: κοινὴ αἴσθησις
ontologyNodes.definition: The common sensibles (figure, magnitude, motion, number) perceived by more than one sense; the faculty of perception that is numerically one but specifically different for each sense-province; perceives time.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Sense and Sensibilia

ontologyNodes.name: αἰτία / αἴτιον
ontologyNodes.definition: Soul is cause in three senses: efficient (*hothen hē kinēsis*), final (*to hou heneka*), and formal (*to ti ēn einai*).

ontologyNodes.name: τέλος
ontologyNodes.definition: Nature acts for an end; all natural bodies are organs of soul; the "for the sake of which" has two senses (end achieved, being in whose interest).

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι
ontologyNodes.definition: Soul as formal cause; "the essence is identical with the cause of its being" -- identity of essence and explanatory ground.

ontologyNodes.name: λόγος
ontologyNodes.definition: Third technical proof: persuasion through demonstrating a truth or apparent truth via the words of the speech. Also: the broader sense of rational speech distinguishing humans from animals. Rhetoric is an offshoot of dialectic, and dialectic operates through λόγος.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: μεσότης
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - De Anima; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: Potentiality / Capacity
ontologyNodes.definition: A starting-point (*arche*) of change in another thing or in the thing itself *qua* other (Theta.1). Includes the capacity for being acted on and the state of insusceptibility to change for the worse. Rational potentialities (sciences, arts) produce contrary effects; non-rational potentialities produce only one. The Megaric denial of unexercised potentialities is refuted. Matter as such is potentiality. The infinite exists only potentially.

ontologyNodes.name: End / Purpose
ontologyNodes.definition: The "that for the sake of which"; the final cause. In Theta.8, actuality is identified with the end — potentiality is acquired for the sake of the actuality. In Lambda, the good functions as final cause for cosmic order. In Delta.16, *teleion* (complete/perfect) is that which has attained its *telos*. The formal and final causes are often the same (Lambda.4).

ontologyNodes.name: Movement / Change
ontologyNodes.definition: General term for any process of change. In Kappa.9 (reproducing Physics III), defined as "the actuality of the potential *qua* potential." Distinguished from *energeia* proper in Theta.6: movements are incomplete (at the same time one is building but has not built), while complete actualities are not (one is seeing and has seen). In Lambda, movement must be eternal because time is eternal; only circular locomotion is continuous and eternal.

ontologyNodes.name: Thought / Intellect
ontologyNodes.definition: In Alpha, Anaxagoras' *nous* is the first clear identification of an efficient cause (though used as a *deus ex machina*). In Lambda, divine thought (*noesis*) is the activity of the unmoved mover — "thought thinking itself" (*noesis noeseos noesis*). Thought and its object are identical in things without matter (Lambda.9). For incomposite substances, truth is "contact" (*thigein*) — direct intellectual apprehension without propositional structure (Theta.10).

ontologyNodes.name: Formula / Account
ontologyNodes.definition: Polysemous: definitional formula, rational account, ratio, speech. In Zeta, the parts of the *logos* are parts of the form, not of the matter. In Theta.2, the rational formula (*logos*) differentiates rational from non-rational potentialities — the rational formula explains both a thing and its privation. The definition (*horismos*) is a *logos* that states the essence.

ontologyNodes.name: Art / Craft
ontologyNodes.definition: Universal knowledge arising from many experiences; knows the "why" not merely the "that" (Alpha.1). One of three sources of generation: in art, the form (*eidos*) is in the soul of the maker — "the medical art is the formula of health" (Z.vii, 1032b1). As a rational productive capacity, art can produce contrary effects (Theta.2).

ontologyNodes.name: State / Having
ontologyNodes.definition: A kind of activity of the haver and the had; a disposition by which a thing is well or ill disposed (Delta.20). The primary contrariety is between state (*hexis*) and privation (*steresis*) (Iota.4). Potentialities acquired by practice or learning require prior exercise and constitute *hexeis* (Theta.5).

ontologyNodes.name: πρὸς ἕν (Focal Meaning)
ontologyNodes.definition: The logical structure by which many senses of "being" relate to one central sense (substance), as "healthy" relates to health (Gamma.2, 1003a33). Resolves the aporia of how a single science can study multivocal "being": being is neither univocal nor equivocal but *pros hen* — said in many ways but always with reference to substance.

ontologyNodes.name: This-ness / Individuality
ontologyNodes.definition: A criterion for substance: being a determinate, separable individual. Together with separability (*choriston*), thought to belong chiefly to substance rather than to matter alone (Z.iii). Substance indicates a "this" not merely a "such" (*toionde*); the universal always indicates a "such" and is therefore excluded from being substance (Z.xiii).

ontologyNodes.name: Principle / Beginning
ontologyNodes.definition: The first point from which a thing is, comes to be, or is known (Delta.1). Six senses enumerated. All causes are archai; potentiality is defined as an arche of change (Theta.1). The unmoved mover is the first arche (Lambda.7).

ontologyNodes.name: The Unmoved Mover
ontologyNodes.translation: that which moves without being moved
ontologyNodes.definition: The eternal, immaterial, purely actual substance that causes eternal circular motion by being the object of desire and thought — "it produces motion by being loved" (Lambda.7, 1072b3). Its substance is pure actuality with no admixture of potentiality or matter. Its activity is thought thinking itself (*noesis noeseos noesis*). God's essential actuality is life most good and eternal. 55 (or 49) subsidiary unmoved movers correspond to celestial spheres.

ontologyNodes.name: Difficulty / Puzzle
ontologyNodes.definition: A philosophical puzzle arising from equally compelling arguments on both sides. The method of first philosophy requires surveying these before proceeding — "like untying knots: one must see the knot before one can undo it" (Beta.1). Fifteen aporiai catalogued in Book Beta set the agenda for the central books.

ontologyNodes.name: Contradiction (PNC)
ontologyNodes.definition: It is impossible for the same attribute to belong and not belong to the same subject at the same time and in the same respect (Gamma.3). Cannot be demonstrated directly but is defended elenchically: anyone who says anything meaningful already presupposes it. Starting-point for all demonstration. Denial collapses the substance/accident distinction.

ontologyNodes.name: practical syllogism
ontologyNodes.definition: The logical structure whereby a universal major premise about the good plus a particular minor premise about present circumstances yields action (not a proposition) as conclusion; "I want to drink, says appetite; this is drink, says sense: straightaway I drink" (701a32-33).

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ ἀγαθόν
ontologyNodes.definition: The final cause that initiates movement; the object of desire; may be actual good, apparent good, or the pleasant; not every intelligible object moves but only the end in the domain of conduct.

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ κινοῦν ἀκίνητον
ontologyNodes.definition: That which causes motion without being moved; in cosmology, the mover of the heavens; in animals, the object of desire as final cause; grounds the requirement for an immovable point in all locomotion.

ontologyNodes.name: σύμφυτον πνεῦμα
ontologyNodes.definition: The bodily medium through which the soul transmits movement to the limbs; capable of expansion and contraction; stands to the soul-origin as the moved joint-point stands to the unmoved.

ontologyNodes.name: ἀλλοίωσις
ontologyNodes.definition: Bodily change (heating/chilling) that mediates between psychological states (phantasia, desire) and locomotion; imaginations produce the same bodily effects as real objects.

ontologyNodes.name: ἐπιθυμία
ontologyNodes.definition: A species of desire directed at the pleasant; operates without deliberation; supplies the major premise in rapid action.

ontologyNodes.name: προαίρεσις
ontologyNodes.definition: Resolve, deliberate choice; acting from out of oneself; distinguished from δόξα in seven respects; constitutive of πρᾶξις and ἕξις.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Movement of Animals; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: χρῶμα
ontologyNodes.definition: The central object of the treatise; simple colours belong to the four elements (white to fire/air/water/earth, yellow to fire/sun, black to transmuted elements); intermediate colours arise from mixture and blending of simple colours in varying proportions.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - On Colours; Aristotle - Sense and Sensibilia

ontologyNodes.name: μῖξις / κρᾶσις
ontologyNodes.definition: The primary mechanism for generating intermediate colours from simple ones; covers both physical mixing of elemental constituents and observational chromatic variation; different strengths yield crimson, violet, grey, brown, flame-colour.

ontologyNodes.name: φῶς / σκότος
ontologyNodes.definition: Light is the colour of fire; darkness is privation of light, not a colour; the interaction of light and darkness with the four elements generates simple colours. Darkness lacks definite magnitude or shape, distinguishing it from black.

ontologyNodes.name: πέψις (maturation)
ontologyNodes.definition: The natural process through which plants and animals undergo chromatic change via heat, nutriment, and moisture; fruit progresses from herb-green through a chromatic sequence; animal hair/feathers change through nutriment cycles. Central explanatory principle for chs. 5-6.

ontologyNodes.name: στοιχεῖα
ontologyNodes.definition: The four elements to which simple colours belong; the material substrate of all colour generation through transmutation and mixture.

ontologyNodes.name: τροφή
ontologyNodes.definition: Determines animal colouring: white when moisture containing proper colouring dries up in maturation; black when moisture settles and becomes stale; explains age-related chromatic changes.

ontologyNodes.name: βαφή
ontologyNodes.definition: The paradigm case of colour transference through moisture and heat entering pores; used as analogy for both fruit maturation and elemental colour change; the dye-fruit analogy is central to ch. 5.

ontologyNodes.name: λαμπρόν
ontologyNodes.definition: Continuity and density of light; explains why gold appears glistening and pigeons' necks appear lustrous; a property of light rather than colour.

ontologyNodes.name: μέλαν / λευκόν
ontologyNodes.definition: The extremes of colour: white is the natural colour of the elements and the colour of deviation and weakness; black is the colour of transmutation. All intermediate colours arise from their mixture.

ontologyNodes.name: μνήμη
ontologyNodes.definition: A state (ἕξις) or affection (πάθος) of perception or conception, conditioned by the lapse of time, directed exclusively at the past; not itself perception or conception but a subsequent dispositional state; belongs essentially to the primary faculty of sense-perception (τὸ πρῶτον αἰσθητικόν).

ontologyNodes.name: ἀνάμνησις
ontologyNodes.definition: A distinct quasi-inferential process (ζήτησις) of recovering memory through the deliberate sequential reactivation of habitual movements; belongs only to beings with the faculty of deliberation (βουλευτικόν); governed by association (succession, similarity, contrariety, contiguity).

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ πρῶτον αἰσθητικόν
ontologyNodes.translation: the primary perceptive faculty / common sense
ontologyNodes.definition: The faculty by which one cognizes magnitude, motion, and time; the organ to which memory essentially belongs; identical with the common sense (κοινὴ αἴσθησις).

ontologyNodes.name: χρόνος
ontologyNodes.definition: The necessary condition of memory: all memory implies the lapse of time; recollection essentially involves the perception of time as magnitude, determinately or indeterminately; only time-perceiving animals can remember.

ontologyNodes.name: τύπος
ontologyNodes.definition: The quasi-physical mark stamped in the soul and its bodily seat by perception; analogous to a seal-ring impression in wax; the quality of this impression explains individual differences in memory.

ontologyNodes.name: ἕξις / πάθος
ontologyNodes.definition: Memory is defined as a ἕξις or πάθος of perception/conception; ἕξις = the settled dispositional condition that persists; πάθος = the modification undergone by the soul and its bodily organ.

ontologyNodes.name: εἰκών
ontologyNodes.definition: The relational aspect of the φάντασμα: when the soul perceives the image *qua* related to something else, it functions as a likeness and enables memory.

ontologyNodes.name: βουλευτικόν
ontologyNodes.definition: The faculty of deliberation; recollection belongs naturally to those who possess it, since recollection is a form of inference.

ontologyNodes.name: ἀρχή
ontologyNodes.definition: The initial term from which the recollective search proceeds; the middle of a series is the optimal starting-point; functions as a psychological τόπος.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - On Memory; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ψόφος
ontologyNodes.definition: The central object of the treatise; all sounds arise from the impact of air against bodies or bodies against air; qualitative differences (hard, soft, clear, rough, thick, thin) are determined by the physical properties of the sound-producing organs and the transmitting air.

ontologyNodes.name: πληγή
ontologyNodes.definition: The fundamental mechanism of all sound production; sound arises when air is set in motion by impact — contraction, expansion, compression, or the blow of breath against bodies; the force and manner of impact determine sound quality.

ontologyNodes.name: πνεῦμα
ontologyNodes.definition: The material cause of vocal sound; its force, quantity, and manner of expulsion from the lungs through the windpipe and mouth determine the qualitative differences among voices (hard, soft, clear, rough, shrill, deep).

ontologyNodes.name: σαφές
ontologyNodes.definition: A quality of sound analogous to clearness in colour; produced by concentrated, solid, and pure stimuli striking the sense organ with maximal penetration; requires that the breath or impact not be dispersed or divided.

ontologyNodes.name: σκληρός / μαλακός
ontologyNodes.definition: Hard sounds strike the hearing with force and travel with added momentum; soft sounds arise from gentle breath. Determined by the force of the impact of breath from the lungs, not the hardness of the windpipe.

ontologyNodes.name: τραχύς
ontologyNodes.definition: Rough sounds arise when the impact of air on the ear is not single but divided and dispersed, each portion striking separately; compared to rough objects touching the skin (cross-modal touch analogy).

ontologyNodes.name: συμφωνία
ontologyNodes.definition: Musical concords arise because overlapping note-impacts cause intermediate sounds to escape notice; the shriller note strikes simultaneously with the slower, producing apparent continuity.

ontologyNodes.name: ὀξύς / βαρύς
ontologyNodes.definition: Pitch distinction: quickness of breathing produces shrillness; slowness of breath or large quantity produces depth.

ontologyNodes.name: παχύς / λεπτός
ontologyNodes.definition: Volume-related: thick sounds produced when breath is emitted in great quantity (men's voices, well-filled oboes); thin when breath is small (children, women, eunuchs).

ontologyNodes.name: Motion / Change
ontologyNodes.definition: "The fulfilment of what is potentially, as such" (201a10--11). The actuality of the potential qua potential — not the completed state but the process of actualizing. Occurs in four categories: substance, quality, quantity, place (200b26--201a3). Strictly, motion is change from subject to subject only (V.1, 225b10); coming-to-be and perishing are changes (metabolai) but not motions.

ontologyNodes.name: Actuality / Fulfilment
ontologyNodes.definition: The actualization or completed state of a capacity. In the definition of motion (III.1), entelecheia names the *process* of actualizing, not the completed state: "the fulfilment of what is potentially, as such, is motion" (201a10). Energeia is used for the priority of form over matter: "a thing is more properly said to be what it is when it exists in actuality" (II.1, 193b7). In VIII, the mover is in actuality what the moved is in potentiality (257a1).

ontologyNodes.name: Potentiality / Power
ontologyNodes.definition: The capacity of a thing to be or to become something. In III.1, motion is the actuality of the potential *as potential*. In III.6, the infinite exists only potentially. In IV.1, place has "power" (dunamis) — natural places attract elements (208b10). In VIII.4, what is potentially X becomes actually X when the hindrance is removed (255b1).

ontologyNodes.name: End / Final Cause
ontologyNodes.translation: end / that for the sake of which
ontologyNodes.definition: The goal or purpose for the sake of which a thing is done or comes to be. "Nature belongs to the class of causes which act for the sake of something" (II.8, 198b10--11). Nature acts for an end without deliberating: spiders, ants, swallows build purposively (199b26--30). Natural necessity is hypothetical: the matter is necessary for the end, not the end for the matter (II.9, 200a5--15).

ontologyNodes.name: The Infinite
ontologyNodes.definition: "Not what has nothing outside it, but what always has something outside it" (III.6, 207a1--2). Exists only potentially and by division, never as an actual completed substance. Its essence is privation; it is a cause in the sense of matter (207b35--208a1). The infinite exists processually, "in the sense in which we say it is day or it is the games" (206a22--24).

ontologyNodes.name: The Continuous
ontologyNodes.definition: That whose parts share a common boundary; infinitely divisible into always-divisible parts (V.3, 227a10--15; VI.1, 231a21--b18). The continuous is the most intimate of the topological relations: succession -> contiguity -> continuity. Nothing continuous is composed of indivisibles.

ontologyNodes.name: The Unmoved Mover / Prime Mover
ontologyNodes.definition: That which first imparts motion without itself being moved. Eternal, exempt from all change (both unqualified and accidental), without parts and without magnitude (VIII.6, 258b11--12; VIII.10, 267b25--26). Causes continuous, uniform circular motion. Situated at the circumference.

ontologyNodes.name: Contraries
ontologyNodes.definition: All change (except circular locomotion) proceeds between contraries (I.5, 188a19--189a10; VIII.8, 261b33). The principles of nature are contraries; motion in a straight line reverses between contraries and must therefore involve rest at turning points.

ontologyNodes.name: Chance / Spontaneity
ontologyNodes.definition: Incidental causes within the sphere of what happens for the sake of something. Chance is restricted to agents capable of choice (II.5, 197a5--8). Spontaneity is the wider genus, including events among animals, children, and inanimate things (II.6, 197a36--b30).

ontologyNodes.name: Locomotion
ontologyNodes.definition: Motion in respect of place. One of three species of motion (V.2, 226b10). Argued to be the primary and most fundamental kind of motion at VIII.7 (260a20--261a27): alteration presupposes locomotion, growth presupposes alteration, locomotion alone does not change the being of the subject. Circular locomotion is the only continuous and infinite locomotion (VIII.8--9).

ontologyNodes.name: Hypothetical Necessity
ontologyNodes.definition: Necessity in nature runs from end to matter, not from matter to end: "the saw must be of iron, if we are to have a saw" (II.9, 200a10--13). "Necessity is in the matter, while that for the sake of which is in the definition" (200a14--15).

ontologyNodes.name: ῥητορική
ontologyNodes.definition: The faculty of observing in any given case the available means of persuasion; counterpart (ἀντίστροφος) of dialectic; universal in scope, belonging to no definite science; an offshoot of dialectic and ethical studies.

ontologyNodes.name: πίστις / πίστεις
ontologyNodes.definition: The means by which persuasion is effected; divided into technical (ἔντεχνοι: ethos, pathos, logos) and non-technical (ἄτεχνοι: laws, witnesses, contracts, tortures, oaths). The enthymeme and example are the two modes of demonstrative pistis.

ontologyNodes.name: ἐνθύμημα
ontologyNodes.definition: The rhetorical syllogism/deduction; "the body (σῶμα) of persuasion"; drawn from probabilities and signs using fewer premises than a full syllogism. Twenty-eight lines of probative enthymeme catalogued (II.23); ten lines of apparent/spurious enthymeme (II.24). Two kinds: demonstrative and refutative.

ontologyNodes.name: πάθος / πάθη
ontologyNodes.definition: "All those feelings that so change men as to affect their judgements, and that are also attended by pain or pleasure" (1378a20). Second technical proof. Each emotion analysed under three heads: (a) state of mind, (b) persons toward whom felt, (c) grounds. Systematic catalogue: anger, calm, friendship, enmity, fear, confidence, shame, kindness, pity, indignation, envy, emulation.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ἦθος
ontologyNodes.definition: First technical proof: persuasion through the speaker's character as projected in the speech itself (not prior reputation). Three sources of trust: good sense (φρόνησις), excellence (ἀρετή), goodwill (εὔνοια). Character types catalogued by age (youth, prime, old age) and fortune (birth, wealth, power). Style must express character-class (III.7).

ontologyNodes.name: λέξις
ontologyNodes.definition: The manner of linguistic expression; second of three points of study (after invention, before arrangement). Excellence consists in clarity (σαφήνεια) through current words combined with distinction through metaphor. Governed by appropriateness (τὸ πρέπον). Art must appear natural.

ontologyNodes.name: μεταφορά
ontologyNodes.definition: The transfer of an alien name to a thing; the supreme instrument of prose style. "Gives clearness, charm, and distinction as nothing else can" (1405a8). Implies "an intuitive perception of the similarity in dissimilars." Must be drawn from kindred things. Materials must be beautiful to ear, understanding, eye. Achieves highest effect through πρὸ ὀμμάτων ποιεῖν (setting before the eyes) via ἐνέργεια.

ontologyNodes.name: πρὸ ὀμμάτων ποιεῖν
ontologyNodes.definition: Metaphor that represents things in a state of activity (ἐνέργεια), making the audience visualize the subject. The culmination of the metaphor theory: the mechanism by which language produces quasi-perceptual experience. Homer paradigmatic.

ontologyNodes.name: τέχνη
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetoric is a τέχνη — a systematic, teachable faculty. Yet its supreme instrument (metaphor) "is not a thing whose use can be taught" (1405a9), and its highest principle demands that art conceal itself (1404b18). The tension between rhetoric as τέχνη and its dependence on natural capacity is constitutive.

ontologyNodes.name: τόπος / τόποι
ontologyNodes.definition: The argumentative "places" from which enthymemes are constructed. Common topics (κοινοὶ τόποι) apply across all three species; special topics (ἴδιοι τόποι) belong to particular subject-matters. Twenty-eight lines of enthymeme are topoi.

ontologyNodes.name: παράδειγμα
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetorical induction; reasoning from particular to particular (like to like). Two varieties: historical parallels and invented parallels (illustrative comparisons and fables). When enthymemes available, examples serve as supplementary witnesses; otherwise primary mode of demonstration.

ontologyNodes.name: γνώμη
ontologyNodes.definition: General statement about practical conduct; constitutes the premiss or conclusion of an enthymeme with the syllogistic element removed. Invests speech with moral character. Appropriate to the elderly and experienced.

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ πρέπον
ontologyNodes.definition: The governing principle of style: language must correspond to emotion, character, and subject-matter. Appropriate language "makes people believe in the truth of your story" (1408a20). Threefold: expressive of πάθη, reflective of ἦθος, matching gravity of subject.

ontologyNodes.name: ἕξις
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetoric is a ἕξις — a settled capacity or disposition, not merely a knack. Virtues are ἕξεις; the orator's character is a ἕξις that must be projected through speech. Links rhetoric to the ethical framework of NE.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: τάξις
ontologyNodes.definition: The ordering of the parts of a speech; third point of study. Only statement (πρόθεσις) and proof (πίστις) strictly necessary. Standard divisions: introduction (προοίμιον), narration (διήγησις), proof, epilogue (ἐπίλογος).

ontologyNodes.name: φρόνησις
ontologyNodes.definition: One of three sources of trust in the speaker's character. Practical intelligence that enables wise decisions. Links rhetoric to the ethical doctrine of NE VI.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: ἀρετή
ontologyNodes.definition: "A faculty of providing and preserving good things, or of conferring many great benefits" (1366a36). Parts: justice, courage, temperance, magnificence, magnanimity, liberality, gentleness, prudence, wisdom. Matter of epideictic oratory. Also one of three sources of trust in character.
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: εὐδαιμονία
ontologyNodes.text: Aristotle - Rhetoric; Heidegger - Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ διαφανές
ontologyNodes.definition: A common nature and power (κοινὴ φύσις καὶ δύναμις) not peculiar to any element but subsisting in all bodies in greater or lesser degree; when actualized by a fiery element it is light; its privation is darkness; colour exists at its limit in determinate bodies.

ontologyNodes.name: μῖξις
ontologyNodes.definition: Genuine blending of ingredients at the level of minimal parts, distinguished from juxtaposition and superposition; Aristotle's preferred explanation of intermediate colour generation and analogous savour generation.

ontologyNodes.name: δύναμις / ἐνέργεια
ontologyNodes.definition: The potential-actual distinction applied to perceptibility: sensible qualities exist potentially in sub-threshold magnitudes and become actually perceptible only at sufficient scale; resolves the infinite-divisibility puzzle.

ontologyNodes.name: φῶς
ontologyNodes.definition: The colour of the transparent incidentally; the actuality of the transparent qua transparent, produced by the presence of a fiery element in the medium.

ontologyNodes.name: χυμός
ontologyNodes.definition: The affection wrought by the sapid dry (τὸ ξηρόν) in the moist (τὸ ὑγρόν), transforming the sense of taste from potentiality to actuality; savour stands to the moist as colour stands to the transparent.

ontologyNodes.name: ὀσμή
ontologyNodes.definition: Analogous to savour but operating through air and water; divided into two species: nutritive odours correlated with savours (shared by all animals) and odours pleasant in their essential nature (perceived only by humans).

ontologyNodes.name: τὰ ἴδια αἰσθητά
ontologyNodes.definition: Objects specific to each sense (colour to sight, sound to hearing, etc.); the senses are not deceived about their proper objects; contrasted with common sensibles.

ontologyNodes.name: μέγεθος
ontologyNodes.definition: Every sensible object is a magnitude; the distance from which it can be perceived is determinate, with an indivisible boundary between imperceptibility and perceptibility.

ontologyNodes.name: παράθεσις
ontologyNodes.definition: Side-by-side placement of white and black in imperceptibly small quantities; rejected hypothesis for intermediate colour generation.

ontologyNodes.name: τὸ ὑγρόν
ontologyNodes.definition: The material substrate in which savour is generated; water as the base medium for taste, analogous to the transparent for colour.

ontologyNodes.name: σκότος
ontologyNodes.definition: The privation of light; the condition of the transparent when the fiery element is absent.

ontologyNodes.name: Being
ontologyNodes.definition: The fundamental theme of the treatise — not a being (Seiendes) but that which determines beings as beings. The question of the meaning of Being (Sinn von Sein) drives the entire inquiry. Not a genus, not definable through traditional logic, yet pre-ontologically understood by Dasein in every comportment toward beings.

ontologyNodes.name: Dasein
ontologyNodes.definition: The entity that each of us is, distinguished by the fact that in its Being this Being is an issue for it. Dasein exists — its essence lies in its existence (to-be). It is characterized by mineness (Jemeinigkeit), being-in-the-world, and the structural totality of care. Dasein is the entity through which the question of Being must be raised.

ontologyNodes.name: Being-in-the-world
ontologyNodes.definition: The unitary, a priori structural whole that constitutes Dasein's basic state. Not a spatial containment but a mode of existing: Dasein is always already "in" a world, engaged with entities, alongside others. Its three structural moments — Being-in, world, the who — are analyzed in Division One and temporally grounded in Division Two.

ontologyNodes.name: Care
ontologyNodes.definition: The structural totality of Dasein's Being, formally articulated as Being-ahead-of-itself-already-in-(the-world)-alongside (entities encountered within-the-world). Unifies the existential moments of existence (understanding/projection), facticity (thrownness/state-of-mind), and falling. Demonstrated through the phenomenon of anxiety, confirmed by the cura fable, and temporally grounded as the meaning of temporality.

ontologyNodes.name: Temporality
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological meaning of care and the primordial horizon for the understanding of Being. Unfolds in three ecstases — future (Zukunft), having-been (Gewesenheit), Present (Gegenwart) — each with an authentic and inauthentic mode. Temporality is not a sequence of "nows" but the ecstatic-horizonal unity that makes possible Dasein's existence, facticity, and falling. Distinguished from Temporalität (temporality of Being as such), which B&T announces but does not fully develop.

ontologyNodes.name: Being-towards-death
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's ownmost, non-relational, not-to-be-outstripped, certain yet indefinite possibility. Death is not an event at the end of life but the possibility of the impossibility of existence — a constitutive structure that individualizes Dasein and opens authentic self-understanding. Anticipation (Vorlaufen) lets Dasein hold open this possibility without fleeing into the "they's" evasive interpretations.

ontologyNodes.name: Disclosedness
ontologyNodes.definition: The "there" (Da) of Dasein — the clearing in which entities can show themselves and Dasein can encounter itself. Equiprimordially constituted by state-of-mind, understanding, and discourse. Disclosedness is more primordial than any propositional truth; it is the existential-ontological condition for truth as unconcealment. Falling both belongs to and conceals this disclosedness.

ontologyNodes.name: Understanding
ontologyNodes.definition: An equiprimordial existentiale of disclosedness (alongside state-of-mind and discourse). Understanding is Dasein's projective grasp of its own potentiality-for-Being and of the Being of entities it encounters. Always has the structure of projection (Entwurf) and discloses possibilities, not merely cognitive contents. Developed in interpretation (Auslegung), which articulates the fore-structure. Temporally grounded in the ecstasis of the future.

ontologyNodes.name: State-of-mind
ontologyNodes.definition: An equiprimordial existentiale of disclosedness that discloses Dasein's thrownness and facticity. Ontically manifested as mood (Stimmung). Every state-of-mind discloses Dasein as already delivered over to its "there" — it reveals the "that it is" while the "whence and whither" remain in darkness. Fear is an inauthentic mode; anxiety is the fundamental mode that discloses Being-in-the-world as such. Temporally grounded in having-been.

ontologyNodes.name: Falling
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's tendency to lose itself in the "they" and in the entities it encounters within-the-world. Not a moral failing or a Fall from a higher state but an essential existential structure: Dasein is proximally and for the most part absorbed in its world. Manifested concretely as idle talk, curiosity, and ambiguity. Characterized by temptation, tranquillizing, alienation, and entanglement (downward plunge). Temporally grounded in inauthentic making-present.

ontologyNodes.name: Das Man
ontologyNodes.definition: The anonymous, everyday "who" of Dasein. Not a particular person or sum of persons but the nobody to whom every Dasein has proximally surrendered itself. The "they" prescribes the kind of Being of everydayness through averageness, levelling down, publicness, and disburdening. Dasein's ownmost self must be wrested from the "they" through individuation (anxiety, conscience, resoluteness).

ontologyNodes.name: Resoluteness
ontologyNodes.definition: The authentic mode of disclosedness in which Dasein, called by conscience and accepting its Being-guilty (nullity), projects itself upon its ownmost potentiality-for-Being. Involves reticence, anxiety-readiness, and the letting of the ownmost Self act from itself. In its full existential form as anticipatory resoluteness (vorlaufende Entschlossenheit), it unites Being-towards-death with the call of conscience, disclosing the Situation as the authentic "there." Temporally grounded as the authentic present (moment of vision, Augenblick).

ontologyNodes.name: Worldhood
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological structure of the world as an existentiale of Dasein, analyzed through the referential totality of significance (Bedeutsamkeit). Not the totality of beings but the relational context (involvement, for-the-sake-of-which) within which entities can be encountered as ready-to-hand. Temporally grounded in the horizonal schema of the ecstases.

ontologyNodes.name: Readiness-to-hand
ontologyNodes.definition: The mode of Being of equipment (Zeug) as encountered in circumspective concern. Equipment is not first perceived as an object with properties (presence-at-hand) and then given a value-predicate; rather, it is encountered as something in-order-to, within a totality of involvements. Readiness-to-hand is ontologically prior to presence-at-hand.

ontologyNodes.name: Presence-at-hand
ontologyNodes.definition: The mode of Being of entities as they show themselves when circumspective concern breaks down or when theoretical attitude takes over. The present-at-hand is an entity stripped of its involvement-character, regarded as a mere "thing" with determinate properties. Traditional ontology (Descartes, the metaphysical tradition) privileges this mode, mistakenly taking it as the primary way of Being.

ontologyNodes.name: Authenticity/Inauthenticity
ontologyNodes.definition: The two fundamental modes in which Dasein can be itself. Authenticity: Dasein owns its existence, projecting upon its ownmost possibilities. Inauthenticity: Dasein disperses itself in the "they," evading its ownmost Being. Both are genuine modes of existence — inauthenticity is not lesser but the proximal and average way Dasein exists. The distinction runs through every existential structure.

ontologyNodes.name: Anxiety
ontologyNodes.definition: The fundamental state-of-mind that discloses Dasein's Being-in-the-world as such. Distinguished from fear: fear has a definite within-the-world object, anxiety does not. In anxiety, the world sinks into insignificance, the "they" collapses, and Dasein is individualized, thrown back upon its ownmost potentiality-for-Being. Reveals the uncanniness (Unheimlichkeit) underlying everydayness. Serves as the methodological access point for the phenomenon of care.

ontologyNodes.name: Conscience
ontologyNodes.definition: The call (Ruf) of care that summons Dasein from its lostness in the "they" to its ownmost Being-guilty. Conscience discloses Dasein's nullity — the constitutive not-Being at the ground of its thrown projection. The caller is Dasein itself in its uncanniness; the called is the they-self. Wanting-to-have-a-conscience is the existentiell choice of resoluteness.

ontologyNodes.name: Discourse
ontologyNodes.definition: The third equiprimordial existentiale of disclosedness (with state-of-mind and understanding). Discourse articulates the intelligibility of Being-in-the-world. It is more primordial than language (Sprache), which is the worldly expression of discourse. Constitutive moments: what discourse is about, what is said, communication, making-known. Includes hearing (Hören) and keeping silent (Schweigen). Falls into idle talk (Gerede) in everydayness.

ontologyNodes.name: Thrownness
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's factical character of being delivered over to its "there." Dasein finds itself always already in a world, with a past and possibilities not of its choosing. Thrownness is disclosed in state-of-mind and constitutes the "already-in" moment of care. In Division Two, thrownness is temporally deepened as having-been (Gewesenheit) and ontologically extended through historicality.

ontologyNodes.name: Spatiality
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's existential spatiality, constituted by de-severance (Ent-fernung, bringing-close) and directionality (Ausrichtung). Not Cartesian extensio but a mode of Being-in-the-world: Dasein de-severs entities by bringing them into the nearness of concern. Grounded in temporality (the ecstasis of making-present) but not reducible to temporality. Space is neither "in" the subject nor "in" the world but discovered through Dasein's spatial Being-in-the-world.

ontologyNodes.name: Historicality
ontologyNodes.definition: Dasein's ontological constitution as historical, grounded in the ecstatic-horizonal temporality of care. Dasein "historizes" (geschieht): it stretches along between birth and death, inheriting a heritage and projecting possibilities that have-been. Authentic historicality is fate (Schicksal) — resolute taking-over of inherited possibilities. Communal historicality is destiny (Geschick). Founds the possibility of historiology as a science.

ontologyNodes.name: Within-time-ness
ontologyNodes.definition: The most derivative level of temporality: time as publicly encountered "in which" events and entities occur. Characterized by datability, significance, spannedness, and publicness. Expressed through reckoning with time and clock-use. When its existential origins are levelled off, within-time-ness degenerates into the "ordinary" concept of time as an infinite, homogeneous sequence of nows (now-time, Jetzt-Zeit). Aristotle's definition of time as the number of motion belongs here.

ontologyNodes.name: Interpretation
ontologyNodes.definition: The working-out of possibilities projected in understanding. Not a bare cognitive act but the articulation of what is understood through the fore-structure: fore-having (Vorhabe), fore-sight (Vorsicht), fore-conception (Vorgriff). The hermeneutical "as" (something as something) is the primordial "as-structure" of interpretation. The apophantical "as" of assertion (Aussage) is a derivative modification.

ontologyNodes.name: Being-with
ontologyNodes.definition: The existential structure through which Dasein is always already with Others. Not an additive relation (subject + subject) but an a priori co-constitution of Being-in-the-world. Others are encountered "from the world" of shared concern, not as present-at-hand objects. Gives rise to solicitude (Fürsorge) in its positive modes (leaping-in/dominating vs. leaping-ahead/liberating).

ontologyNodes.name: Destruktion
ontologyNodes.definition: The critical dismantling of the traditional concepts of ontology to lay bare the original experiences from which they arose. Not destruction in the negative sense but a positive appropriation that loosens the hardened tradition. Targets Kant, Descartes, Aristotle as stations. Only partially carried out in B&T; announced in the Introduction as the second task of the treatise.

ontologyNodes.name: Existence
ontologyNodes.definition: The kind of Being toward which Dasein can comport itself and always does comport itself somehow. Dasein's "essence" lies in its existence — it is what it can be. Distinguished from the traditional existentia (actuality, presence-at-hand of an entity). Existentialia are the Being-characters of Dasein; categories belong to non-Dasein entities.

ontologyNodes.name: Fear
ontologyNodes.definition: An inauthentic mode of state-of-mind with a definite threatening entity (Wovor), a specific threatened entity (Worum), and a particular way of fearing. Distinguished from anxiety, which has no definite within-the-world object. Fear flees from a definite threat; anxiety discloses Being-in-the-world as such.

ontologyNodes.name: Signs
ontologyNodes.definition: A particular kind of equipment whose function is to indicate — to make a referential totality conspicuous. Signs serve circumspection by orienting Dasein within its environment. Analyzed as a case study in the structure of reference (Verweisung) and worldhood.

ontologyNodes.name: Idle talk
ontologyNodes.definition: The everyday mode of discourse in which communication spreads and repeats what is said without genuine appropriation. Language becomes groundless — understanding floats free of the things themselves. One of the three concrete modes of falling (with curiosity and ambiguity).

ontologyNodes.name: Curiosity
ontologyNodes.definition: The everyday mode of seeing that seeks novelty for its own sake, never dwelling but always moving on. A fallen mode of circumspection freed from its practical context. Traced to Aristotle's wonder but shown to be its inauthentic derivative.

ontologyNodes.name: Phenomenology
ontologyNodes.definition: The method of the treatise: "To let that which shows itself be seen from itself in the very way in which it shows itself from itself." Composed of phenomenon (that which shows itself) and logos (letting something be seen). Phenomenology is ontology — access to the question of Being requires the phenomenological method. Hermeneutical in character: an interpretive uncovering.

ontologyNodes.name: Reality
ontologyNodes.definition: Traditionally identified with the Being of entities (res). Heidegger argues Reality is ontologically grounded in care: "Reality" as a mode of Being of within-the-world entities presupposes Being-in-the-world. Neither the independence of the "external world" nor realism vs. idealism can be resolved without first clarifying the Being of the entity that raises such questions. Resistance (Widerständigkeit) reveals Reality in practical coping, not in theoretical perception.

ontologyNodes.name: Circumspection
ontologyNodes.definition: The kind of sight (Sicht) belonging to practical concern with ready-to-hand entities. Not theoretical observation but a looking-around that guides Dasein's handling of equipment. When circumspection encounters breakdown (conspicuousness, obtrusiveness, obstinacy), the ready-to-hand entity begins to show itself as present-at-hand.

ontologyNodes.name: Selfhood
ontologyNodes.definition: The existential-ontological constitution of Dasein's self-constancy (Selbst-ständigkeit). Not a persisting substance (soul, subject, person) but grounded in the ecstatic unity of temporality. Authentic Selfhood: Self-constancy in anticipatory resoluteness. Inauthentic selfhood: the they-self's lack of Self-constancy (un-Selbst-ständigkeit).

ontologyNodes.name: Temporalität
ontologyNodes.definition: The temporality of Being itself — distinguished from Zeitlichkeit (temporality of Dasein). The projected but unfinished horizon of the treatise: B&T demonstrates Zeitlichkeit but only announces Temporalität as the answer to the question of the meaning of Being in general. The unpublished Division Three was to have worked this out. Remains the "open question" of the book.

ontologyNodes.name: Ambience / Ambient
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological condition in which the surrounding environment is not a passive container or backdrop but an active, generative, immersive ground from which things, meanings, and rhetorical situations emerge. Ambience is less driven by connection (as in networks) and more resonant with immersion, permeation, and osmosis. It names the dynamic, emergent ecology of coadapting elements -- human, nonhuman, material, technological, environmental -- that compose the world prior to and exceeding any subject-object division.

ontologyNodes.name: Ambient Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetoric reconceived as the always-ongoing disclosure of the world that shifts our manner of being in that world, rather than a discrete symbolic act performed by autonomous human agents upon passive audiences. Ambient rhetoric encompasses material things, nonhuman agencies, ecological assemblages, attunement, and the withdrawal of objects from relation. It is "disclosure itself becoming affective, suasive" (Conclusion, 281) and is fundamentally preparatory rather than paradigmatic.

ontologyNodes.name: Attunement / Stimmung
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's ontological concept of mood (*Stimmung*) reconceived as the fundamental disclosure of the world that precedes cognition, volition, and intention. Attunement is not a subjective state of mind or willed comportment but "an ambient catalysis within what is most material and concrete, a gathering that springs forward" (Ch2, 98). It is "like an atmosphere in which we first immerse ourselves in each case and which then attunes us through and through" (*FCM* 67). Attunement grounds ambient rhetoric as the condition under which things, situations, and persuasive forces show up at all.

ontologyNodes.name: Disclosure / Aletheia
ontologyNodes.definition: The Heideggerian concept of truth as unconcealment: things come to presence in a particular way, always also concealing other aspects. Disclosure is always ongoing, never exhaustive, and never solely the doing of human beings. In Rickert's culminating formulation, "rhetoric is ambience as affective disclosure" (Conclusion, 281). Every act of unconcealing is simultaneously a concealing, which means rhetoric must attend to what withdraws as well as what appears.

ontologyNodes.name: Dwelling
ontologyNodes.definition: Not mere habitation but an ontological, ecological relationship between humans, things, and environments. Dwelling is "activity conditioned by the land and the things of the world" (Ch7, 243) -- the ongoing process of building, disclosure, and attunement through which humans and nonhumans coexist. "Dwelling built the farmhouse, not the peasants per se" (Ch7, 243). Dwelling is the mode through which affectability becomes rhetoric conceived ambiently, and it is inherently ethical insofar as it gives rise to values through practice rather than human projection.

ontologyNodes.name: Ecology
ontologyNodes.definition: The relational, mutually constitutive field of human and nonhuman elements, opposed to "environment" understood as a passive container. Derived from Greek *oikos* (household/dwelling place), ecology names the condition in which things, organisms, materials, and practices condition and support one another. Rhetoric is ecological insofar as its action is "material, affective, ecological, and emergent" (Ch3, 129).

ontologyNodes.name: Fourfold
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's gathering of earth, sky, divinities, and mortals in things. Not four separate categories but a "onefold" in which each element mirrors and rings in the others, constituting an ongoing interplay of presence and withdrawal. The fourfold is lived first and philosophized second; it is the framework through which dwelling takes its bearings. Things "gather" the fourfold, as in the jug example where wine, water, spring, earth, and sky are all gathered in the poured gift.

ontologyNodes.name: Rhetorical Being
ontologyNodes.definition: The condition of being-in-the-world as inherently rhetorical -- not a rhetorical agent who deploys persuasive techniques but a being whose very existence is constituted by the ambient disclosure of world. Rhetoric is not something one does but something one is immersed in. Rhetorical being names "the synthesis of multiple content threads of varying intensities" (Ch4, 133) gathered within material and affective environments.

ontologyNodes.name: Thing / Gathering
ontologyNodes.definition: A thing is not a mere object but a gathering of concerns, relations, and situations. Etymologically, Old English *thing*/*ting* = assembly for deliberation; Latin *res* = matter of discourse; the Icelandic *Althing* = parliament. Things gather the fourfold and participate in rhetoric as material agents of disclosure. The "rhetorical thing" (Ch6) names material participants in the ambient disclosure of world -- not merely objects of persuasion but co-constituents of rhetorical situations.

ontologyNodes.name: Chora
ontologyNodes.definition: The Platonic "third kind" (*triton genos*) from the *Timaeus* -- neither Form nor material copy but a generative, withdrawing matrix or receptacle from which all becoming, beginning, and creation emerge. Rickert recovers *chora* through Kristeva (semiotic/affective), Derrida (deconstructive/aporetic), and Ulmer (inventional/performative) to show that rhetoric and invention rest on an "infomaterial" ground that reveals and conceals simultaneously. The *chora* is the ancient precursor to ambience: "Place is not simply an immediate environment; it includes the background by means of which things show up" (Ch1, 55).

ontologyNodes.name: Kairos
ontologyNodes.definition: Traced from its earliest Greek usage as a spatial-material concept (a penetrable opening on the body, a gap in the warp of a loom) through its Sophistic elaboration as temporal opportunism, to Rickert's ambient reframing. Ambiently understood, kairos names the emergent disclosure of a situation in which rhetor, environment, and occasion co-constitute one another. Kairos "wills" the human (via Miller/Untersteiner/Heidegger), not the other way around; it aligns with complexity theory's "tipping point" where a system transforms.

ontologyNodes.name: Nonhuman Agency
ontologyNodes.definition: Agency distributed across human and nonhuman actants -- not a projection of human agency onto objects but an acknowledgment of their performative operationality emergent from material, contextual, and relational conditions. Theorized through Latour's actant concept, Harman's tool-being, Bennett's vital materialism, and Brooks's subsumption architecture. Material things exercise persuasion irreducible to symbolic mediation (speed bumps, Berlin Key, electrical grid).

ontologyNodes.name: Embodiment / Embodied Cognition
ontologyNodes.definition: The condition of being bodily situated in and constituted by a material environment. Drawing on Clark's extended cognition, Dourish's embodied interaction, and Heidegger's being-in-the-world, Rickert argues that minds are "at once embodied and dispersed into the environment" -- composites of intellect, body, information, and material scaffoldings. Embodiment grounds the ambient claim that rhetoric is material, not merely symbolic.

ontologyNodes.name: Invention
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetorical invention reconceived as fundamentally emplaced -- arising not from autonomous rational method but from the generative matrix of material, affective, and environmental relations. Invention is something that happens *through* the coinvention of subject, place, and circumstance. Kristeva's *chora* shows invention exceeds the range of symbolicity; Ulmer's chorography practically enacts choric invention; Verbal Kint demonstrates "inventive passivity before the ambient environs."

ontologyNodes.name: Worldliness / Being-in-the-World
ontologyNodes.definition: Heidegger's foundational claim that Dasein is always already thrown into a world of practical involvements -- not a subject confronting objects but a being immersed in meaningful situations. From this ground, language, rhetoric, and invention emerge. Worldliness means that the world is simultaneously material and meaningful, never exhausted by the presence of material things, and rhetoric is "a response to the way the world attunes and speaks us" (Ch5, 189).

ontologyNodes.name: Withdrawal
ontologyNodes.definition: The ontological condition whereby objects, meanings, and the world itself are never fully present to any relation. Things always reserve depths that exceed human knowledge, use, and attribution. Withdrawal is not absence but "a form of supporting" (Ch7, 244) -- the condition of possibility for ongoing disclosure. It ensures that the world is always more than what we make of it. Theorized through Harman's tool-being, Heidegger's concealment, and the *chora*'s generative recession.

ontologyNodes.name: Networks
ontologyNodes.definition: Treated as ontological rather than merely technological -- "a principle of being" in which subjects emerge as nodular points within coadaptive threads (via Taylor's complexity theory). However, Rickert argues the network metaphor is necessary but insufficient for ambient rhetoric because it remains invested in binaries (node/link, foreground/background) and lacks the immersive, osmotic, material thickness that ambience requires. Ambience supplements and exceeds the network.

ontologyNodes.name: Periechon
ontologyNodes.definition: Greek term meaning "that which surrounds, encompasses, or makes room for." Appears alongside *chora* in Plato's *Timaeus* and connects to the sense of a surrounding cosmos that is itself alive. Rickert identifies it as the ancient Greek precursor to the concept of ambience and returns to it in the book's final sentence as what ambient rhetoric recovers: "a renewed sensibility to what the ancient Greeks called *periechon*" (Conclusion, 285).

ontologyNodes.name: Technics / Technology
ontologyNodes.definition: Technology understood not merely as instrumental tool but as disclosive -- it reveals how we are in the world (connecting to Heidegger's *Question Concerning Technology*). Rickert maintains a dual stance: technology makes ambient conditions newly visible (Eno, ambientROOM, EV1), yet technological solutions to technologically produced problems risk entrenching us deeper in technological thinking (enframing). The *chora* dissolves the *techne*/*physis* distinction.

ontologyNodes.name: Terroir
ontologyNodes.definition: The irreducible somewhereness of wine rooted in earth, climate, practice, and place. Serves as the book's governing figure from the Preface onward, returned to in the Conclusion as a "material-social-hermeneutic ecology." Terroir grounds the claim that rhetoric, like winemaking, is constituted by material relations that exceed human intention and control.

ontologyNodes.name: Sufficiency
ontologyNodes.definition: Not a countervalue to be adopted but an ontological attunement materialized through dwelling practices. Opposed to the ambient logic of efficiency that pervades modern life. Sufficiency "emerges as a principle only insofar as we can abstract it from already ongoing dwelling" (Ch8, 257). Demonstrated through Toronto Island's resistance to automobility.

ontologyNodes.name: Electracy
ontologyNodes.definition: Ulmer's term for the emerging cultural epoch shaped by electronic media, analogous to literacy's relation to print. Electracy is itself choric -- "a third kind, following but being neither progress from nor a hybrid of orality and literacy" (Ch1, 68). New media and ambient intelligence make choric invention's emplaced, distributed character newly visible.

ontologyNodes.name: Soundmarks
ontologyNodes.definition: R. Murray Schafer's term for the sonic counterpart to landmarks -- culturally valued sounds that define and organize communities. Distinguished from keynotes (ambient background sounds) and signals (meaningful foreground sounds). Used in Ch4 to demonstrate that sound is woven into the fabric of dwelling and rhetoric, not ornamental addition.

ontologyNodes.name: Assemblage
ontologyNodes.definition: Bennett's term (via Deleuze): a historical, contingent grouping of disparate actants generating power along a continuum, vitally inserted into larger assemblages that exceed and conflict with constituent actants. The university, the electrical grid, Toronto Island are all assemblages. Extends Latour's actant concept by emphasizing nested complexity and uneven power distribution.

ontologyNodes.name: Preparatory Rhetoric
ontologyNodes.definition: Rhetoric conceived not as direct persuasion but as groundwork that lays conditions for disclosure and transformed dwelling. The book itself is "ultimately only preparatory" (Ch8, 269). Ambient rhetoric "cannot short-circuit itself into being a new paradigm" but can only attune, lay groundwork, and open conditions of possibility.
